message.content:
{
  "decision": "APPLY",
  "workflow_yaml": "name: Node.js CI

on: [push, pull_request]

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5

    strategy:
      matrix:
        node-version: [18, 20, 22]

    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: ./web

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@11bd71901bbe5b1630ceea73d27597364c9af683 # v4.2.2
        with:
          submodules: recursive
      - name: Find any lock file
        run: if test -f ../yarn.lock || test -f ../pnpm-lock.yaml || test -f ../package-lock.json; then echo "Please don't commit lock files" && exit 1; fi
      - name: Use Node.js ${{ matrix.node-version }}
        uses: actions/setup-node@49933ea5288caeca8642d1e84afbd3f7d6820020 # v4.4.0
        with:
          node-version: ${{ matrix.node-version }}
      - run: yarn install --ignore-engines
      - name: Build FE for production test
        working-directory: ./web/frontend
        run: yarn install --ignore-engines && yarn build
",
  "rationale": "Add a custom job timeout of 5 minutes to the build job. The pattern P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT (literature simulation estimate) reports VM time reductions of 12.9% (free) and 8.1% (paid) by bounding jobs with an explicit timeout. The experiment example (batch-interactive-three--fb8b16eb65a11508) measured a 26.8% elapsed time reduction on a forked workflow when adding a 5-minute timeout. This repository's historical CI runs complete in 45-75 seconds, so a 5-minute timeout provides generous headroom while preventing runaway executions. The change is minimal, preserves all matrix configurations and test coverage, and does not weaken permissions or add privileged actions.",
  "evidence_ids": ["pattern:P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT", "experiment:batch-interactive-three--fb8b16eb65a11508"]
}

```yaml
      - name: Find any lock file

          node-version: ${{ matrix.node-version }}
      - run: yarn install --ignore-engines

        working-directory: ./web/frontend
        run: yarn install --ignore-engines && yarn build
```
